title: OST crackles under heavy loading
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.52-dev (25 October 2026), not built yet: the first load after the intro movie ran the music dry 1-3 times (v0.0.51-dev3 and the final: 0 late, every other load 0 dry). Cause: the music stream reads its next 16 KiB block only from the frame loop (CDAudio_Update) or as the painter's emergency fill; a load holds the frame loop, and the track restarted after the movie with an empty buffer. Now every load-time mixer update (snd_dma.c S_Update_) also pumps the stream's reads (aw_music.c AW_MusicLoadPump, never waits; not under the movie); tests: music_player_test loadpump, aga_loading_audio_test. To verify: the audio smoke of the next dev build, the first load 0 dry, and the maintainer's WinUAE listen. Before: Corrected 25 October 2026 (v0.0.51-dev, not built yet): the first load's 219-319 ms 'gap' and its dry count in the dev1 and dev2 measurements were the intro movie, which plays inside the New Game load, pauses the music and plays its own sound; the load meter timed the paused music. The meter now leaves the movie out and says so, and names the load step at both ends of the longest gap (a trace of the ticks when it passes 150 ms). Measured again (FS-UAE, 32 MB, the dev2 image with the gate 3891 engine, the same five loads): longest gaps 58 (first load, outside a 4,893 ms movie), 43, 52, 115 (Akulakhan's Chamber, world model to entities) and 49 ms, 0 late. The first load still counts the music running dry 3 times outside the movie (likely the music restarting after it; not checked). Before: Fixed in part in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing; WinUAE listen pending. Ordinary file and model reads already read in 4 KiB slices with the music serviced between them; the CHIM pack reads (rooms, frames, models: one read of up to megabytes) did not, and now do. Every load prints 'Loading audio: N mixer updates, longest gap X ms (mixes Y ms ahead), K late, music ran dry D times'. FS-UAE, 32 MB, same five loads before/after: longest gap Seyda Neen 216/221, prison ship 39/37, census office 55/52, Akulakhan's Chamber 218/204, Balmora 205/46 ms; the mixer mixes 1,486 ms ahead; 0 late in every load. The remaining ~200 ms gaps in Seyda Neen and the chamber are another step of those loads. The opening's crackle (hull to deck, census office) is judged by the maintainer on WinUAE with the v0.0.51 playtest, where the console prints the same lines
where: Music mixer during heavy loads (ship hull to deck, entering Census office)
severity_reason: The music never crackling through loads is the project s golden standard (the maintainer, 24 October 2026); the opening is the first thing every player hears

title: Every NPC appearance is baked whole: shared body parts are converted again for each actor, and equipment cannot change
status: PERSISTING in v0.0.48-rc1 (24 October 2026): stage 1 of docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md (parts library, gallery from parts) is built; stage 2 (residents from the library) and stage 3 (the engine composed-model loader) were never built, and v0.0.48 baked the 1,769 interior residents whole, every one with its own 64 animation frames: the rc1 image carries about 1,500 MB of actor models against 297 MB for Morrowind.bsa (ROOM-RESIDENT-MODELS-SIZE-48). Stages 2 and 3 come first in v0.0.49 (docs/ROADMAP.md, "The actors get the CHIM rule"). The maintainer (2026-10-25 17:28 +0200 / 2026-10-25 15:28 UTC, TG 17:27): 'the whole idea is that they all used the shared lookup table for actions... we need shared lookup tables for common actions, that is the point'. The animations are baked per actor too: every mover holds its own walk, run and attack frames (992 MB of the 1.5 GB of actors in v0.0.51), so the region actors got no movers at all (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35). Wanted: one shared animation table per skeleton, the body parts as a library, each actor composed and skinned once at load (docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md stages 2-3); first measure the load-time skinning cost of one town on the 68030/68040 target. Raised to the v0.0.52 list after the door table (DOOR-ENTRANCE-AUDIT-51). Progress (2026-10-25 21:20 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:20 UTC, v0.0.52 Skeletons Of Society, method C in docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the shared humanoid table holds every group (139 of 139, the combat phases and the inventory poses included; walking, running, sneaking, swimming and jumping held in place); the engine reads the table and a model s skeletal block and poses it per drawn frame (aw_skel.c, r_alias.c), the protocol carries frames past 255 (U_AW_EXT AWU_FRAME2); the first real skeletal actor, a Balmora resident, is 359,184 bytes for every motion against 395,700 for today s idle-only bake (plus a mover of about 501 KB), engine pose within 0.20 model units of the baked frames at idle (the two-bone joint blend up to 1.24 units in run and death poses); box 66 x 81 x 41 units, 0 of 5,046 frames clamped. Open: SKEL-VERTEX-LIMIT-52, SKEL-TABLE-SIZE-52, the game logic for every group (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35), the in-game prototype and SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52. Payload plan (2026-10-25 21:34 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:34 UTC; the maintainer: the disk space is insane, it should not be in the package): skeletons alone remove the 992 MB of baked frames and the second (mover) model, but each character s mesh and skin stay stored once per character (about two thirds skin): about 1,770 characters x about 360 KB, roughly 600 MB. The parts library (each body part once, measured at about 67 MB for every resident against about 535 MB baked whole) assembled at load is the other half: v0.0.52 takes both, with a hard actor budget in the size ledger. Ship rule (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: would that include the 990 MB of prebaked frames in the game? No): from v0.0.52 a shipped build carries no baked actor frames and no mover models; the baked method is a test-build option only (the animation stage A/B, a few MB); a kit check refuses a shipped build that has them. Default (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: skeletons by default, they take a fraction; whoever wants the prebaked frames compiles the game with them): --npc-anim-type 2 is the builder default; 1 only when chosen at build time. Design (2026-10-25 21:58 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:58 UTC, the maintainer: can the reused modules carry the movement; baking is impossible once actors change clothes): parts carry no motion; 479 of 519 rigid parts drawn with their one bone s matrix (Quake-style, the cost of a static model), about 40 skin parts take the joint blend; the motion is the one shared table. Movement sets per part would be per-part baking, the same mistake; a baked actor cannot change clothes without a bake per outfit. docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md Getting NPC movement right. Measured again (2026-10-25 23:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:54 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try3): the boot payload is 3,028,309,475 bytes, id1/progs 1,996,183,591 of it (the baked actors and their mover models): 820 units had to move off DH0 onto the world volumes. Builder (2026-10-26 00:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:54 UTC, v0.0.52, method C step C3): --npc-anim-type 1 or 2 in tools/build.py, default 2 (skeletal); 1 = the baked kit exactly as before. Type 2: every humanoid resident (prepare_area.build_resident: towns, Seyda Neen, rooms) and actor-library model (npc_library) is one rest frame on the shared table of its skeleton (progs/humanoid.awsk; progs/humanoid_f.awsk, the female groups layered over the common ones as OpenMW stacks xbase_anim_female over xbase_anim; progs/humanoid_kna.awsk, the beasts), each written once; the kit layout names the table's frames; no mover models, no baked frames; the type is in the resident stages' keys (AMIWIND_NPC_ANIM_TYPE) and the actor library's appearance keys. Size ledger (the base game's 2,612 placed NPC records, the react+full profile, files before resident sharing): type 1 3,222 MB for the 2,515 it bakes (models 1,256 MB, movers 1,957 MB), type 2 512 MB for the same 2,515 plus 1.8 MB of tables (about 1,281 KB against 204 KB an actor); docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md. Open: the in-game check, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52, the kit check that refuses baked frames in a shipped build, the parts library (the skins and meshes per character are what is left). Kit check (2026-10-26 01:44 +0200 / 2026-10-25 23:44 UTC): the release guard (the kit tooling) refuses a v0.0.52-or-later release whose image build does not record npc_anim_type 2 (build-state.json, written by tools/build.py since 471cadcd): no baked actor frames in a shipped build. To confirm on the dev1-try5 build state once written.

title: Roads and paths on the ground look blocky: each texture square is drawn with hard edges instead of blending into its neighbours
status: Reported 18 October 2026 by the maintainer ('the road paths look like shit atm'; every path of the game): a path breaks into separate squares instead of reading as one track. Morrowind's land texture layer is 16 x 16 squares per cell and blends neighbouring squares; ours draws one texture per square with hard edges. Planned A/B, first option the maintainer's (20:04): (d) DIAGONAL SPLITS: where a square's texture meets a different texture on two adjacent sides (a corner of a stair-step edge), split that square along its diagonal into two triangles, each with one texture, so stair-steps become 45-degree edges (marching-squares over the texture grid; about one extra face per split square, no new textures). Then, if needed: (a) baked transition textures for the edge pairs that occur, (b) a dithered edge band baked into the surfaces, (c) finer squares along roads. Measured in faces, memory and frame time; OpenMW at the same pose.
where: Ascadian Isles, cell 1,-4 (global 15133 -31424 931): roads and paths island-wide

title: The player cannot climb the walkway at the Vivec Hlaalu canton dock and gets stuck
status: Cause measured 18 October 2026: both spots (2,-11 ref 278930; 4,-11 ref 278913) are ex_v_dock_01. mesh_geometry.collision_parts built each convex collision piece from its extreme points along 14 directions; on the dock deck (level, then sloped) that hull lies up to 19.4 units under the planks the authored collision follows (dev2 frame at the first spot: collision 143.8, planks 160.8). The dev3 stair fix does not change it. Island-wide: 535 exterior meshes have walkable collision more than a step over their pieces. Fix (branch v0.0.43-dockwalk): the 484 measured meshes of config/collision-hull-surface.json keep all points of a piece whose reduced hull leaves its source more than 0.5 units outside (68,666 placements; hull bytes 1.06 to 1.63 MB stored once; at most +110 KB at a frame heap peak, no frame over budget on the dev2 world); a collision surface gate checks every CHIM mesh. Branch brought up to the v0.0.45 dev line 20 October 2026; verification waits for a build.

title: Entering Akulakhan s Chamber (the Heart Chamber) ends the game: a model of its room store does not load, and the engine stops with Host_Error instead of refusing at the door
status: Cause found and fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: 32 MB got no automatic cache bank (CHIM-AUTO-BANK-CLIFF-51), so the room's 10.1 MiB of models did not fit. With the repaired engine dbg tp heartchamber at 32 MB loads the room in play (365 placements, 135 models, 5.0 s). Open part: a room that cannot load during play still stops at the console instead of refusing at the door PERSISTING in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev2_dev2_3715e8c4). Seyda Neen, then Balmora (dbg cam recall bm3), then dbg tp heartchamber ended in Host_Error: CHIM room map maps/rifa4ef181ed.chim: its room record or models cannot be loaded. The room found 2 MiB of the free Fast RAM for its models (and 1994 KiB of the Hunk) and a model of the store could not be loaded. Afterwards: Memory now 4795 KiB free, largest block 4492 KiB. Loaded as the first map it works: 4 MiB taken, Memory now 1291 KiB free, largest block 1177 KiB, zone 1476 KiB free. The difference was the skeletal session memory held since the town: the animation tables and the large pose cache, 1589 KiB. Fixed in 2d49fb88 (gate 4032): before Chim_RoomGrow measures the free Fast RAM, the engine flushes its skeletal models from the model cache and gives back the tables and the large pose cache, all made again on demand (aw_skel_release.c). Checked on a play copy of the dev2 image with the 2d49fb88 engine swapped in: the same route loads the chamber (1589 KiB given back first, 3 MiB of Fast RAM and 1994 KiB of the Hunk taken, room 148 models 18129 KiB loaded in 2701 ms). Afterwards Memory now is 2200 KiB free, largest block 2058 KiB; the zone has 420 KiB free, largest run 417 KiB. The Heart's structure and a figure before it are in view. Still open at 32 MB: 2 model loads fail both after the town and as the first map (zone failed requests, the last 250624 bytes after the town, 60112 as the first map); at 64 MB 0 fail. Which models these are (Dagoth Ur's full model and the Heart's actor are the suspects, outside the build gate's count) is not identified yet. Stills: clips/v0.0.52 akulakhan_chamber_32mb_after_balmora, 32mb_first_map, 64mb_after_balmora. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: named and fixed (v0.0.52, gate 4034). The two failed loads at 32 MB were not models left out: zone failed: model 1639 (x/ex_dwrv_enter00, a Dwemer entrance of the room, 250,580 bytes) and model 4991 (i/in_akulacave00 tile 5,8, 147,092 bytes) are the requests that made the room grow (try 1 full, the free Fast RAM bank; try 2 full, the Hunk rest; try 3 loaded): every model was in place (room: 148 models, 18,129 KiB; zone used = the gate's need), neither Dagoth Ur (an actor model in Quake's cache, not the zone) nor the Heart. The console now says so (room: loaded whole on try 3; it grew 2 times, each after a request the full zone refused). The real shortfall was the margin: after Balmora the room bank was 3 MiB (zone 420 KiB free) because the tables given back do not join the largest block and the bank was cut to whole MiB. Fixed: the room bank in 64 KiB steps (CHIM_ROOM_GRAIN); a registry of re-makeable session memory (aw_fastrelease.c AW_FastReleaseRegister/AW_FastReleaseAll, 8 releasers, one console line each with free and largest block before and after) called before the CHIM cache banks at start-up, -chimcache and a room's growth (never per frame), the skeletal tables and posed frames its first releaser; a console line of the free Fast RAM at the room step. Measured at 32 MB after Balmora (FS-UAE, dev2 image, new engine): given back 1,589 KiB, free 4,696 -> 6,286 KiB, largest 4,488 -> 5,512 KiB, bank 3,456 KiB (was 3,072), zone 804 KiB free (was 420), Memory now 1,814 KiB free, largest 1,671. The room heap gate counts the worse route now (engine_limits MEASURED_ROOM 5,512 KiB: bank 3,456 KiB; the chamber needs 19,093,616 of 19,968,800, its walk leaves 848 KiB, measured 804) and the actors: the animation tables their skeletal models name and the pose cache must fit what the room bank leaves (CHIM_ROOM_KEEP 2 MiB), else the gate fails (the chamber: humanoid table 579,816 + pose cache 393,984 = 990,188 bytes). Tests: tests/test_fast_release.py (native registry with stubs, call sites, every MEMF_LARGEST sizing listed), aga_chim_world_test roomgrow, test_chim_room_heap; m68k 4 variants clean. 2026-10-26 13:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 11:02 UTC: committed 9741c99c (gate 4034 passed, 5,913 tests); in-game check in the dev3 image.

title: The chim stage's read record is always incomplete: it starts compilers with checkout paths, so it can never be reused when only its key's sources changed
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (25 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: the trace hook writes what a C compiler (cc, gcc, m68k-amigaos-gcc, clang) reads of the checkout: the sources on its command line, also a temporary one outside it, and their #include closure through its -I folders (^ lines); the record counts them as data and is complete. Found with it: a compile with relative paths in the checkout named no checkout path, so its record counted as complete with none of what it read. Tests: tests/test_build_cache.py CompilerReadsTests
where: tools/chim/zone_sim.py build_library and check_world_map_heap's ABI probe (gcc with checkout paths)
severity_reason: Any change in the chim stage's key sources, even to files it never used, rebuilds the CHIM world (about 40 minutes)
platform_reason: builder reuse records

title: The pool map that hands results back in input order scans every held future on each turn: the main process works O(n squared) while large maps run
status: Open (25 October 2026): found profiling the main process of a cached CHIM validation on the v0.0.51-dev1 world (22 workers): ordered_map 8.2 s of its own, Future.done 5.2 million calls (4 s), the _running count 3.8 million (3.5 s). With a cost every item is submitted largest first, so pending holds every result not yet handed back (up to all 1351); each loop turn counts the running ones over all of pending (_running) and builds the wait list over all of pending. Repair: count and wait only on the submitted-and-running set (at most the limit). Not done yet: ordered_map is not a scheduling unit, so any edit re-keys every stage and per-unit cache that reaches it (the NPC gallery faces, the stair data: a build that walks stairs is barred). First make the dispatch loop a scheduling unit with a new key form (BUILD-KEY-RULE-NO-FORM-51), then repair it
where: tools/build_parallel.py ordered_map (_running, the wait list)
severity_reason: About 16 s of the main process in every CHIM validation, more in every large map with a cost; the workers wait on it

title: An interior light change reran exterior stages: the reuse cutoff refuses a stage when any earlier stage's whole output differs, not the files it reads
status: Open (25 October 2026): v0.0.51-dev3 changed only tools/interior_lighting.py (and the engine). The reuse preflight planned 26 of 43 stages reused, 0 unexpected; at run time 12 of them were refused by the output cutoff (npcs, hands, npc-gallery, world-flora-assets, harvest, hand-catalog, door-audio, character, reading, world-ui, actor-contact, world-terrain), because bsp, census and the other room stages now bake different light. The legacy scene chain is one ordered line (tools/build_parallel.py DEPENDENCIES: bsp, npcs, hands, ... world-ui, actor-contact, world-terrain), and world-flora-assets, harvest and hand-catalog follow census only for its palette (BUILD-PALETTE-RACE-32), yet census.bsp's new light refuses them. The read trace records checkout reads only, never run-folder reads, so the cutoff cannot narrow to what a stage opened. Repair: record each stage's run-folder reads with their SHA-256 and refuse only when one of those differs (whole-output compare kept as the fallback for records without them); the preflight then names the stages that follow a rebuilt stage's outputs as conditional, not as reused Seen again (2026-10-26 00:17 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:17 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try4): an engine change confined to aw_items.h (a parser prototype) and aw_skel.h (the table struct) rebuilt world-flora, chim and chim-town-seyda, whose keys hold every engine header they compile for the struct sizes of their heap checks; the sizes they measure did not change. Key those stages on the measured sizes (compile_target_sizes output) instead of the header sources.
where: tools/build_cache.py apply_stage (output cutoff) and tools/build_parallel.py DEPENDENCIES
severity_reason: A room light change reruns exterior and character stages, and the start-up plan does not show it (26 planned reused, 14 reused)
platform_reason: A builder reuse fault, seen in the dev3 build log; no game run involved

title: The cell sunlight is baked as brightness only: Akulakhan's Chamber is lit grey where the original lights it red
status: Open (25 October 2026): the v0.0.51-dev3 heart chamber shots (FS-UAE, 32 MB, four directions from the arrival point) show the room readable, no longer near black (INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-UNBAKED-51), but grey-brown; the cell's sunlight is 255,140,140, a strong red, and the bake takes only its luma. The bake already gives warm lamps a warm lightstyle (WARM_STYLE, R_SurfaceWarm); a tinted style per cell sunlight colour, or the room's dominant light colour, is the candidate. Judge against the original/OpenMW at the arrival pose. Census of the three masters (25 October 2026): sunlight tinted (strongest channel at least 1.5x the weakest) in 896 of 1,335 interior cells (604 red/orange, 140 yellow, 83 green, 69 blue/purple), and in 222 of them the tinted sunlight is the main light (at least 2x the ambient luma); 630 of 676 light records are tinted (447 red/orange, 129 blue/purple, 30 green, 24 yellow), and only warm lamps get a tint today; fog tinted in 762 cells Engine side in source (2026-10-25 15:15 +0200 / 2026-10-25 13:15 UTC, gate 3915): world format 0.13 gives a CHIM placement a light tint in its record flags bits 2-4 (0 none, 1 warm = aw_light_hue, 2 red, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green, 6 cool blue-white, 7 purple); its faces are built through that tint's colour table (16 KB, made from the palette the first time a map draws the tint, r_sky.c R_BuildTints) and the surface cache keys on the tint as it does on the level (d_surf.c); aw_warm_light 0 turns tints off. Test: tests/aga_chim_placement_light_test.c (record decode 12/13, table choice, cache key) and tests/test_chim_placement_light_native.py. Next: the builder writes the tint (tools/chim/interior.py, from the cell sunlight and the dominant light colour, format 0.13), then a dev build and the heart chamber shots against the original. Builder side in source (2026-10-25 15:21 +0200 / 2026-10-25 13:21 UTC, gate 3916): tools/chim/interior.py writes CHIM rooms as world format 0.13 with a tint per placement from interior_lighting.point_colour (the same ambient, sunlight and light terms as point_light, in colour; its luma is point_light) classified by light_tint (strongest channel at least 1.4x the weakest; hue bands to the seven engine tints); the rooms receipt counts light_tints per room. Tests: tests/test_chim_interior.py LightTintTests. Next: a dev build, then the heart chamber and the census office against the original.

title: The skeletal prototype poses every vertex twice a drawn frame, with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions each: it must cost what a baked frame costs
status: Open (method C, docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the first working version poses an actor s vertices into a scratch frame (bone matrix, quantised with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions, which the 68040 has no hardware instruction for) and the alias path then transforms them again: about twice today s per-vertex work, every drawn frame, estimated at several ms per 1,500-vertex actor on a 25 MHz 68040 (not measured). The method itself costs what baked frames cost: (1) fold each bone s matrix into the one per-vertex transform (view x model x bone, the light direction turned into each bone s space once), so each vertex is transformed once, no divisions or conversions; (2) pose an actor only when its frame changes (alias frames change about 10 times a second, drawn frames 20 to 30); (3) actors on the same table frame share the bone pose; (4) far actors pose less often and skip the joint blend. Acceptance: the frame time of the MiniWind animation stage (SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52) and of CHIM Balmora on the slow-CPU preset no worse than with today s baked actors. Render plan (2026-10-25 22:11 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:11 UTC, after reading AmiQuake s r_alias.c and r_main.c): the actor stays one entity (one box, one light sample, one dynamic light pass, the existing triangle drawing); per bone one combined view x model x bone matrix and the light direction in bone space; the builder sorts vertices by bone so the inner loop keeps one matrix per run (a rigid vertex = a baked vertex s work); pose only on a table-frame change (about 8 a second, a few thousand float operations per actor a second); per-frame ready-made matrices would cost 1.9 to 3.8 MB for the common table and are not worth it; blending between table frames can be switched off (nearest frame). A part that looks wrong rigid and costs too much blended may keep a small shared baked deformation, measured. Progress (2026-10-25 23:46 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:46 UTC): (1) r_alias.c keeps posed frames (8 slots, least recently drawn out; key model, header place, table frame): an actor is posed only when its table frame changes (about 8 a second against 20 to 30 draws) and actors of one model on one frame share the pose; every other draw is a baked frame's work. (2) AW_SkelPoseVerts folds each bone's matrix once with the rest scale and the alias quantisation: per vertex one 3 x 4 transform per bone used, no division; the byte rounding adds 1.5 x 2^23 and reads the mantissa instead of a float-to-integer conversion (the 68040 has no FINTRZ: it traps into the emulation). Native tests within one byte of the builder; compiles for 68040 and 68060 at -O1 and -O2. Not yet measured on the slow-CPU preset (the animation stage). Measured (2026-10-26 05:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:57 UTC, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52): the same MiniWind stage built twice from 7064ea39, --npc-anim-type 1 (baked) and 2 (skeletal). Both ran on the slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 at x14, 49.7 MHz), 32 MB Fast RAM, the Balmora arrival pose at 09:09 with the residents in their own idle (no stage), aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Baked: alias 25.7 ms median (25.6 to 26.0) for 2 alias models drawn, view 1,134 ms, frame 1,261 ms. Skeletal: alias 33.7 ms median (33.5 to 76.0) for 3 alias models drawn, view 1,142 ms, frame 1,271 ms; the 4 lines at about 76 ms are the seconds in which the residents' idle stepped to a new table frame (posing). Per drawn model that is 12.8 ms baked against 11.2 ms skeletal when drawn from the pose cache and about 25 ms when posed. The whole frame was 9 ms (0.7 %) slower at the median and up to 57 ms (4.5 %) slower when posing. Not like for like in one respect: the skeletal build drew one more alias model at this pose (al 3 against 2). Acceptance not met yet: posing costs about twice a baked frame per model. The animated stage (8 actors cycling) on the slow preset is not measured yet. Profiled and cut (2026-10-26 09:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 07:57 UTC). Setup: dbg rcount times the posing (b16bb912: RT_SKELPOSE and RT_SKELVERTS inside the alias time, the kp field with poses made and pose-cache hits), slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 x14), 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Before (b16bb912): one pose was 0.80 ms of bones (AW_SkelPose) and 13.2 ms of vertices (AW_SkelPoseVerts), about 14 ms in all; the vertices are 94 % of it. 871d87e6: a whole frame takes its one key with no blend, square root or division; the never-moving bones are made once per table; the vertex loop has its transforms written out on direct i16 reads. A pose is now 0.61 ms of bones and 9.5 ms of vertices (-28 %). Also fixed there: a forced animation stood still on a slow machine (frames over 0.5 s gave dt 0). 38d6c751: 32 posed frames when AW_TryMalloc allows (the 8 kept slots at 16 MB), so idle residents (an 8-frame loop) stop posing after their first loop. Like for like on one HEAD (3715e8c4), the same pose: baked (--npc-anim-type 1) alias 25.7 ms median, frame 1,272 ms; skeletal alias 33.2 ms, frame 1,275 ms (+0.2 %), with 0 poses in every sampled second. The skeletal side drew 3 alias models against 2 (the extra one passes the cull, likely on the skeletal model's larger box: nothing more is visible in the stills), so per drawn model it is 11.1 ms skeletal against 12.8 ms baked. Worst case, the stage with 8 actors changing group every frame: 8 poses a frame at 0.62 + 8.8 ms each, alias 293 ms against 216 ms held, frame 1.73 s against 1.64 s (+5.6 %). Open: the skeletal box that admits an off-screen actor, and the posing itself (vertices about 8.8 ms a pose on the slow preset). Cull box fixed and remeasured. 685fb2f3 (gate 4031) culls a skeletal actor by the box of the pose it stands in: each posed frame in the pose cache keeps its vertices' box, and the cull uses it once the frame has been posed (before that, the rest frame's every-pose box). Like for like, slow-CPU preset, 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, 15 lines each. Skeletal (stage build 685fb2f3): 2 alias models drawn (the same as baked), alias 25.1 ms median, frame 1,261 ms (one line at 2.2 s), 0 poses and 2 pose-cache hits a second. Baked (3715e8c4, --npc-anim-type 1): 2 models, alias 25.7 ms, frame 1,272 ms. Skeletal is now no slower than baked at this pose (alias -2 %, frame -0.9 %). Open: only the worst case, 8 actors changing group every frame (+5.6 %, about 8.8 ms of vertices a pose).

title: Akulakhan s Chamber needs 18.8 MB for its models and textures with its activators kept: more than the 14.3 MB the 32 MB minimum gives a room, so the image step stops
status: Fixed in source on v0.0.52 (commit d0d2f04b, gate 3944, 25 October 2026), the dev1 build to confirm: a room map holds nothing but its room (the maintainer: just that place and Dagoth Ur), so a CHIM room whose models do not fit its zone and the cache bank now grows under the loading plaque (engine/aga/src/chim/chim_world.c Chim_RoomGrow, chim_room.c ChimRoom_Begin): first a bank of the free Fast RAM (its largest block less 2 MiB, whole MiB), then the game heap s rest past its zone (chim_reserve_kib and what the map loads after the zone kept), both given back at the next map; rooms that fit take neither. Measured in FS-UAE at 32 MB in a room map (the v0.0.51 final image, Akulakhan s Chamber with Dagoth Ur): 6,222 KiB of free Fast RAM in one block, so a 4 MiB room bank; the heap s rest adds 2,094,736 bytes. The image s room heap gate (tools/chim/heap.py) now counts the same steps and the engine s own blocks (the record with its 379 placements, every model and texture, the store index, the prefetch table) and loads a room past one bank through the engine s own allocator (tools/chim/room_zone.py): Akulakhan s Chamber needs 19,093,616 bytes, 32 MB gives a room 20,625,040 (was 14,336,000), 1.53 MB to spare, every model kept (the Heart and Akulakhan); Dagoth Ur s actor model 768 KB at most in Quake s cache, within the 2 MiB gap. All 1,132 rooms of the stopped image pass; 25 are marked for 32 MB (18 before: the store index and the placements were not counted). title: Skeletal actors draw no carried weapon, shield or torch: the item tags hold one row per model frame, and a skeletal model has every table frame
status: In progress (2026-10-26 00:02 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:02 UTC): a per-frame row for all 2,730 table frames would be about 230 KB of text per armed actor. New tag form AWTS1 (the builder: the item paths, the weapon and shield bone indices in the table, the actor scale): the engine (aw_items.c AW_ItemsParseSkel, 93f0272c) poses the table at the actor s frame and makes the row from the bone (aw_skel.c AW_SkelBoneTag, equal to npc_items.quake_angles within 0.002 degrees; its angles from a polynomial atan, since the library s atan2/asin compile to FATAN/FASIN, which the 68040 lacks and the engine audit refused in gate 3946). Open: the builder writing AWTS1 for skeletal residents; the guard torches on the same path; the in-game check. Builder side (2026-10-26 00:13 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:13 UTC): every armed skeletal resident gets its AWTS1 tag (tools/skeletal_actor.py skeletal_tag: the item model paths, the table's weapon bone and shield bone indices, the actor scale; read_skeletal_tag reads it back, tests/test_npc_anim_type.py); the item models are written as before. Still a release blocker for type 2 until the guard torches are on the same path and both are seen in the game. Guard torches (2026-10-26 00:43 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:43 UTC): today prepare_guard_torches.py bakes a body and a held torch model per guard type (8 or 21 frames) and a per-frame flame table (gfx/guard-torches.awg), another per-actor bake that does not fit skeletal guards. Design for type 2: the torch is the guard s shield-slot item in its AWTS1 tag (the item model carries the carried-light rotation and BoneOffset, so its frame is the shield bone s), with an optional line emitter x y z: the torch s fire emitter point in the shield bone s space; the engine places the flame and its light from the item pose each frame (aw_guard_torch.c for skeletal guards). The AWG1 registry stays for type 1 only. Guard torches, builder side (2026-10-26 00:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:54 UTC): a torch-carrying guard (prepare_guard_torches.guard_eligibility) baked skeletal names the torch item on a 'light PATH' line beside its own shield (prepare_guard_torches.torch_item: the original 238 triangles in the shield bone's axes, carried-light rotation and BoneOffset applied; the engine shows it by the day and night cycle) and an 'emitter X Y Z' line after it (the fire emitter point in the shield bone's space, unscaled) in its AWTS1 tag; the image step's guard torch registry (AWG1) leaves skeletal guards out (skeletal_actor.is_skeletal). Checked on the base game's data: 12 torch-carrying guard records; company guard_unique and hlaalu guard bake with weapon, torch and emitter. Open: the engine drawing the flame and light from the item pose (aw_guard_torch.c), the in-game check. Seen in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 3715e8c4): at 22:00 in Balmora (bm1, dbg set time 2200, the automatic cycle: Guard torches auto, automatic night) a skeletal Hlaalu guard staged before the camera (dbg animkit stage 3: common table, weapon, shield, carried light) holds no torch and casts no light. A few flame-like pixels lie on the ground to his left, about his height away. The torch entity or its flame point is placed away from his shield bone. The baked guard registry reported 4 eligible and 4 admitted. Stills and a 15 s clip: clips/v0.0.52 balmora_night_skeletal_guard (with a headlamp-on zoom). Not looked into yet: the guard in his own place (not moved by the stage), and whether the torch model is drawn at all. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: the night torch, checked with a guard in his own place (Seyda Neen sn1, 22:00, automatic cycle; guard lights active 2): real. The torch was drawn as a horizontal stick from the left hand with its flame particles falling beside him. Two causes, both fixed in the engine (gate 4034): (1) the skeletal guard kept his arm down: the baked guards hold the torch with the left arm (Bip01 L Clavicle down) on the table's torch group (prepare_guard_torches.TorchLayer), the skeletal pose did not; the table's shield bone matched the NIF exactly (checked on the maintainer's data), so the item was right and the arm wrong. Now AW_SkelPoseLayer poses the left arm from the torch group (frames 667-688 of humanoid.awsk, in turn with the actor's frame) while torches are shown, for the drawn model, its cull box and the item rows (aw_items.c AW_ItemsTorchLayer; the arm root found as the shield bone's fourth ancestor beside the weapon bone's, no builder change). (2) The flame point was used in the shield bone's units in the item's 0.25-scale space, about three torch lengths out: now taken at the item scale. title: Two skeletal residents found no standing spot in their CHIM rooms: the rest frame soles came out unlike the baked idle soles
status: Found 2026-10-26 04:33 +0200 / 2026-10-26 02:33 UTC in dev1-try8 (2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_dev1-try8_9d4c05f7): the image step actor placement gate stopped on 2 unresolved cases, Hefadmir (Nord, base_anim, reference 299235, room ri16a0c0eea6, soles 2.67 to 3.86 units above support or unsupported) and Wusha (Argonian, base_animkna, reference 280101, room ridbab470875); the CHIM room actor bake had tried all 28,917 spots and refused both, where dev1-try4 (the baked kit) fitted them 12 and 14 units from their authored spots on sloped floors. Not a beast-table fault (Hefadmir is a Nord). Cause, measured with the room fitter on the try8 rooms: (1) the skeletal model was reduced from the 8 idle samples alone, the baked kit from every pose of its profile, so the reduced soles differ (Wusha: other sole points in the half-unit band); (2) its quantisation box spans every table frame, so its z grid fell where it fell and the soles came out up to a step above their true height, the check then taking in points 0.5 above them (Hefadmir: soles spread 0.5 units in height against the baked idle 0.15). Fixed in source: skeletal_resident reduces from the baked kit own samples (npc_anim.plan, the first sample the rest pose), and the z grid puts the rest pose lowest point on a step (skeletal_actor.ground_grid). Rebaked on the maintainer data, both fit their try8 rooms (Hefadmir at attempt 1,514, Wusha at 2,623) and the packaged check passes at the fitted spots (sole gaps -0.48 to 0.99). Tests: test_skeletal_actor (the rest frame on its true soles), test_npc_anim_type (reduced from the kit poses). Open: seen in the next dev1 build.

title: A reused stage recreates, as empty folders, the folders another stage filled beside it: the area stage then stops on its own room folder
status: Found 2026-10-26 05:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:18 UTC in dev1-try9 (2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_dev1-try9_9a95fb79, reusing try8): the area stage stopped in build_room, FileExistsError on intro-scene/area-work/tradehouse. The folder held no file: all 167 folders of the try8 area-work tree (58 rooms) were made empty within 0.1 s as the area stage started. Cause: in try8 chim-room-batches (its roots include intro-scene) ran beside the area stage and saw the room folders appear; Recorder.close gave the shared files to the traced writer (the area stage, BUILD-REUSE-ATTRIBUTION-33) but left the folders in the observer record, so the chim-room-batches reuse plan (2,959 folders) made them (apply_stage, plan directories) and the area stage room build, which creates its folder with exist_ok False, stopped. title: The toolchain's malloc never returns NULL: a failed allocation stops the game with Software Failure #80000027 (TRAP #7); 45 engine malloc sites test for a NULL that cannot come
status: Open (2026-10-26 06:15 +0200 / 2026-10-26 04:15 UTC, found by SKEL-16MB-TRAP-52): libc malloc.o of the Amiga SDK (MemMap::alloc, used by malloc, calloc, realloc and the C library's own buffers) makes a request over 32,747 bytes with AllocMem(size + 4), and a smaller one from 32,760-byte pool blocks. When AllocMem returns NULL it stores through it, a path the compiler turned into trap #7, so no allocation failure ever reaches the caller. The engine has 45 malloc calls outside aw_skel_load.c that test for NULL (aw_actors.c, aw_character.c, aw_glut.c voice table, aw_items.c, aw_cam.c, aw_gallery.c, aw_aread.c and others); each one is a Software Failure on a full machine instead of its message. The guard torch probe already uses AllocMem for this reason (aw_guard_torch.c), and the animation tables now check AvailMem first (484e3455). Wanted: one engine allocator for every malloc that can fail (AllocVec with a tracked list freed at exit, or an AvailMem check), and a test that no engine file calls malloc directly. Progress (2026-10-26 07:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:02 UTC): engine/aga/src/aw_tryalloc.h AW_TryMalloc (e9fb0407, gate 3981) is the allocator that can say no. Its rule matches the toolchain allocator's: a request over 32,747 bytes needs a block of size + 4, a smaller one needs a 32,760-byte pool block, and 16 KB is kept spare. The save buffers (aw_save.c) use it, and the animation tables have their own check (aw_skel_load.c, 484e3455). The other malloc sites are still open. Fixed in e1ab51c5 (2026-10-26 07:47 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:47 UTC, gate 3992): all 45 engine malloc, calloc and realloc calls in 31 files (engine/aga/src and chim/) go through aw_tryalloc. The new aw_tryalloc.c, in the Makefile, holds AW_TryMalloc, AW_TryCalloc (refuses a count x size overflow) and AW_TryRealloc (NULL keeps the old block). Each asks exec's largest free block for what the toolchain allocator will ask (size + 4 over 32,747 bytes, else a 32,760-byte pool block) plus 16 KB, and returns NULL otherwise. The checked versions are used only on the m68k target (AMIGA and __m68k__): a host test that compiles snd_amiga.c with -DAMIGA and stub headers gets the C library's own. Every caller already handled NULL except the playback-argument path in host.c, which now stops with a message. tests/test_engine_allocations.py fails on any malloc, calloc, realloc or strdup call outside comments and strings in any engine .c, .h or .inc; the allow-list is aw_tryalloc.c and the host macros in aw_tryalloc.h. The source-pinned heap policies were re-pinned (tools/alias_stream_heap.py, edge_cache_heap.py, compact_harvest_heap.py). Also: the Skeletal model ... rest pose line is said once per model, not on every load from the cache. The 16 MB FS-UAE check on a stage build of e1ab51c5 follows. Checked (2026-10-26 07:58 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:58 UTC): stage build 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_miniwind-anim-stage-type2_e1ab51c5, FS-UAE JIT at 16 MB. The scripted session passed (105 s): Balmora loaded, the beast table was refused (no memory for 654324 bytes, largest free block 251736) and said once, the arrival autosave was skipped with its message, and the stage lined up its cast. A second session with the UAE monitor's breakpoint on the TRAP #7 handler (trap_run.sh) loaded Balmora and played without reaching it.
where: the Amiga SDK libc malloc.o (MemMap::alloc) and every engine malloc call
severity_reason: Any allocation that fails on a full machine stops the game with a Software Failure instead of a message
platform: FS-UAE 3.1.66, A1200 68040, 16 MB Fast RAM (the SDK allocator read with objdump)

title: A stage whose last real run restored its units from a cache was reused after the code those units come from changed: chim-room-batches kept actor models of the old animation tables
status: Found 2026-10-26 06:29 +0200 / 2026-10-26 04:29 UTC in dev1-try11 (28046c31, reusing try10): the image step stopped on Room batches collide with the image: progs/a_*.mdl and .tag staged with other bytes. chim-room-batches was reused (fingerprint fdd5a1e1, unchanged) although 28046c31 changed tools/skeletal_actor.py and tools/npc_anim.py, which bake its residents (prepare_area.populate): both files are in its closure, but the key covers only the functions its last real run called, and that run restored its residents from the resident unit cache, so the changed table functions (game_table, table_choice, table_groups) were never called and are not in the key. title: A public build can die halfway when the disk fills: the only space check runs once at the start, against a fixed 20 GiB, not what the release really takes
status: Reported by a tester (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26): their v0.0.50 build from the public repository stopped when the disk ran out; the free-space check runs only before the first stage and asks a fixed 20 GiB (AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB), however much the build needs. The maintainer: a gate check from the start, compared with the release s own build size, automatically against the previous known good build with about 20 % extra. Fix: every passing build records its measured full-build footprint (peak bytes of the workspace, the caches and the scratch, per file system); the release ships the last known good build s figure in the repository; before any stage the preflight asks for that figure plus 20 % on each file system and stops with the numbers when it is short; each stage checks its own last measured bytes plus 20 % before it starts; a gate test fails when the shipped footprint is missing or older than the release. The maintainer (2026-10-26 15:20 +0200 / 2026-10-26 13:20 UTC): the margin about 30 % or more, depending on the dependencies; the need counts everything a fresh build takes, not only the workspace: the builder images (about 2.2 GB each), the Morrowind game data copied into the Docker volume, the caches, the storage pool and the scratch. Measured 2026-10-26: the build runs alone take 19 GB (v0.0.51 final) and 16 GB (v0.0.52-dev3), on top of the shared pool and caches. Fix written (2026-10-26 19:45 +0200 / 2026-10-26 17:45 UTC, v0.0.53 builder, branch v0.0.53-disk): tools/disk_need.py. The check runs first in every image build (tools/build.py right after the options are read: build.sh, build.cmd and the build inside Docker), before the builder image is built (tools/build_docker.py, where Docker storage is visible from the host) and before the game data is copied into a volume (tools/run_docker.py, checked inside the image); and before each stage against that stage's own last figure (tools/build_profile.py start). The need per file system: the last known good build's figure (the larger of the shipped config/disk-footprint.json and this workspace's newest passing build) plus disk_margin_percent (30), less the cache and pool when the workspace already holds a passing build's, the workspace never below min_free_gib (35); both in config/build-defaults.json as machine settings that key no stage (tools/build_cache.py keys that file without them; AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB, AMIWIND_DISK_MARGIN_PERCENT and AMIWIND_DISK_WATCH were keyed environment before: now ignored), also --min-free-gib and --disk-margin-percent. Every passing build writes RUN/disk-footprint.json (run folder bytes, scratch peak from the free space sampled every 5 s, cache and pool growth, game data, per-stage peak growth); tools/disk_need.py ship RUN puts it into the repository. First figure, measured read-only on the build volume: the v0.0.52 final's run folder 15.47 GiB (dev3 the same), storage pool objects written in the v0.0.52 cycle 28.84 GiB (an over-count), game data 1.79 GiB, builder image 2.0 GiB: a fresh native build needs about 58 GiB, Docker about 63 GiB. Gate tests: tests/test_disk_need.py (no stage re-keyed by the settings, a stage stops before it starts, a passing build writes its figure, the shipped figure exists and is not older than the release, the guides state the need). Open until a build writes the first measured figure with stage figures. Gate 4048 (2026-10-26 20:14 +0200 / 2026-10-26 18:14 UTC) stopped on tests/test_run_docker (a missing --input-volume must be refused before any Docker run): the volume check now runs right before the game data copy when there is one, otherwise right after the input checks and before the build container is made.
where: tools/build_preflight.py free_space_problems (fixed 20 GiB), tools/build.py
severity_reason: A tester lost a whole v0.0.50 build to a full disk partway through; nothing told them up front
platform: a tester s own Linux machine, public v0.0.50

title: With a graphics card installed the engine picks an RTG screen, then draws it through the slow generic path: the direct CyberGraphX copy is switched off
status: From a tester s minimal RTG patch (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26; private copy, not merged): VID_Init opens cybergraphics.library and, when it is there, asks BestCModeIDTags for an RTG mode, so is_cyber_mode is set; VID_Update then sends the frame through WritePixelArray8 (a one-row planar bitmap per rect) because the direct WritePixelArray RECTFMT_LUT8 call is inside #if 0, and that disabled call passed rects->width as the source modulo where the buffer row (vid.rowbytes) is right. The bootcheck also refuses a machine without AGA. Not confirmed on our side yet: needs the virtual graphics card (UAEgfx) with Picasso96 on the emulated Amiga. Scope (roadmap, RTG beside AGA): AGA stays the default where AGA exists; RTG when there is no AGA or when chosen; the upload from Fast RAM (not drawing into card memory) is the design the roadmap measures first.
where: engine/aga/src/vid_amiga.c: VID_Init mode choice, VID_Update (#if 0)
severity_reason: Any Amiga or emulator with cybergraphics.library gets the RTG screen at its slowest; AGA machines without it are not touched
platform: read in the code; a tester s A3000 RTG build

title: 50 region-frame entrances cannot be used from where a player can stand: the use ray meets the entrance structure or the ground before the door, or there is no standing spot at it
status: Open (2026-10-26 21:58 +0200 / 2026-10-26 19:58 UTC): found by the new wall check of tools/door_engine_check.py on the v0.0.53-dev2 image. 50 of the 830 region-frame exterior entrances cannot be used from any spot a player can stand on in front of them (straight out from the door's face and toward the room's way-out arrival, at the 56-unit use reach and nearer, looking at the middle, upper and lower part): the use ray meets another placement 1 to 33 units before the door (21: the Daedric shrine oval doors of Kaushtarari, Zergonipal, Assurdirapal, Ebernanit, Ashalmimilkala, Bal Ur, Ashalmawia, Maelkashishi, Assarnatamat, Bal Fell; the Rethan and Indarys Manor fort doors; the End of the World renter rooms; the Neglected Shipwreck cabin), no standing spot within 48 units above the threshold (18: Dwemer ruin doors of Arkngthand, Nchuleft, Dagoth Ur Outer Facility, Sorkvild's Tower; Redoran guard tower and outpost trapdoors; Sarys and Odirniran tombs), the ground in front of the door within the ray (9: Velothi tombs and caves such as Andas, Orethi, Senim, Mababi, Sargon, Zenarbael, Endusal, Bthungthumz) or out of reach (2). Seen in game the same evening (FS-UAE, dev2): Kaushtarari and Ebernanit shrines (no prompt; the player stops 63 units from the door), Sadrith Mora Gateway Inn North Wing (no prompt, the ground 13 units above the threshold) and Arkngthand (the use ray meets the doorway arch 8 units before the door; the ground in front lies over the door's lower part). The original LAND at these doors is at the threshold, so the blocking is in the converted collision of the entrance structures and the ground in front of them, not in the original. The full list: door-engine-check.md of the build (private). The count of usable doors with the wall traced (1,052) is in config/door-check-baseline.json and may only go up. 2026-10-26 23:15 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:15 UTC: fixed in source for 40 of the 50. Cause of the largest class: the converted collision of an entrance (the Daedric shrine oval doorways, the Rethan and Indarys fort doors, the End of the World renter rooms, the Neglected Shipwreck cabin; the doorway of some Velothi tombs and caves) closes the doorway 1 to 11 units in front of the door's use box, and aw_scene.c aimed_door refused the use when any surface lay more than 1 unit before the box. Now the doorway slack DOOR_USE_SLACK (16 units) lets the use ray meet a surface that near before the door; a wall farther out still refuses it (tests/aga_scene_test.c: 8 units passes, 24 refused; fails on e088083d's aw_scene.c). The door engine check reads the engine's value and its standing model was made closer to the game (a player may stand up to 80 units over the threshold on the doorway structure itself, and on a trapdoor). On the v0.0.53-dev2 image with the new rule: 1,092 of 1,102 usable with the wall traced (was 1,052), all 1,102 after walking in. The CHIM world is not re-keyed: the change is in the engine and the check only. The 10 left are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53 (v0.0.54). 2026-10-26 23:37 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:37 UTC: in game on the dev2 image with gate 4068's engine (the doorway slack): the Gateway Inn North Wing (Sadrith Mora) and Arkngthand now prompt and enter (the use ray meets their doorway 12 and 7 units before the door); Kaushtarari and Ebernanit still do not: the player slides back down the shrine steps to 62 units from the door, out of the 56-unit reach. The door engine check now also requires a walkable floor where the player stands (Quake's 0.7 normal) and tries spots beside the line out from the door; like for like on the dev2 image: 1,036 usable with the wall traced with the old 1-unit rule, 1,067 with the doorway slack (+31). The 35 left, among them every Daedric shrine whose steps slide, are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53 (v0.0.54). Shipped in v0.0.53 (2026-10-26 23:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:53 UTC): the doorway slack is in; all 1,102 entrances usable after walking in and both ways, 1,067 with the wall traced (+31). The 35 left are DOOR-USE-COLLISION-FILLED-53, v0.0.54.
where: CHIM region frames: collision at exterior load doors (aw_scene.c aimed_door wall trace)
severity_reason: Doors the player cannot enter: Daedric shrines, Dwemer ruins, tombs, forts and guard towers, 50 of 830 region-frame entrances

title: The GitHub source check of v0.0.52 was cancelled at its 25-minute limit: the source-and-dry-run job outgrew it
status: GitHub run 129 (v0.0.52 on main, 08aed75e, the tree of f8a46185) was cancelled after 25m 21s: source-and-dry-run hit timeout-minutes 25 (v0.0.51 took 20m 24s; v0.0.52 adds the skeletal work and its tests, 5,919 in the local suite). No test failed before the cancel. v0.0.52 patch on main (157add5b): the limit raised to 45 minutes. Why so slow (the maintainer, 2026-10-26 20:22 +0200 / 2026-10-26 18:22 UTC: "HOW THE HELL IS IT THAT SLOW ANYWAY!"): one job on one 4-core runner did everything in a row: the bootstrap of every public tool from nothing, the whole suite, the engine compile, the image and its package. Fix on the v0.0.53 line (2026-10-26 21:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 19:02 UTC): the workflow is split into jobs: tools (the bootstrap kept in the Actions cache, keyed by the installer code, its pins and download lists and the runner image; a key change bootstraps from nothing; a restored copy is checked file by file against the manifest of its bootstrap), source-checks, tests (the suite in 6 parallel shards: tools/run_tests.py --shard I/N, whole modules balanced by tests/module-timings.json, every module in exactly one shard, checked by the runner and by tests/test_ci_workflow.py), dry-run (after the tests) and tools-from-nothing (tags, weekly, on request: the from-nothing bootstrap and the dry-run image without any cache); every job has its own timeout-minutes. Open until the first GitHub run of v0.0.53 passes and its job times are recorded in the CI duration record.
where: .github/workflows/source-check.yml (jobs, timeouts), tools/run_tests.py --shard, tools/ci_tools.py
severity_reason: The release commit shows a cancelled check on GitHub; the suite itself had not failed

title: 35 region-frame entrances cannot be reached through their converted collision: 24 Daedric shrine steps the player slides off, raised trapdoors under their tower hulls, Dwemer doors inside the terrain chunk
status: Open (2026-10-26 23:15 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:15 UTC), scheduled for v0.0.54: the 10 region-frame entrances the door engine check still finds unusable after the doorway slack of DOOR-USE-BLOCKED-53, all with converted collision filling the space a player needs at the door. Seven raised trapdoors: the Redoran guard towers of Ald-ruhn (2) and Maar Gan (3), the Ald Velothi outpost and the Indarys Manor fort (Raram's House): the tower's or fort's own collision is solid from 2 to 44 units above the trapdoor, so no player fits over it (column probe of the CHIM collision, point and standing hulls). Two Dwemer doors (Nchuleft, Bthungthumz): the frame's terrain chunk collision stands 90 to 124 units over the door's threshold where the original LAND is at the threshold, so the door is inside the ground. One Telvanni door (Tel Uvirith, Arelas' House): the stronghold's collision fills the space in front of it. Next: check each against the original (OpenMW) and fix the collision conversion (the chunk terrain near doors, the tower and fort hulls), not the doors one by one; the door engine check's usable count (1,092, config/door-check-baseline.json) then goes up to 1,102. 2026-10-26 23:37 +0200 / 2026-10-26 21:37 UTC: with the walkable-floor rule in the door engine check (confirmed in game at Kaushtarari and Ebernanit, where the player slides back down the shrine steps), the count is 35, not 10: 24 Daedric shrine doors whose step collision is steeper than the walk (Kaushtarari, Shashpilamat, Zergonipal, Assurdirapal, Ularradallaku, Ebernanit, Assurnabitashpi (2), Yasammidan, Yansirramus, Ramimilk, Kushtashpi, Bal Ur (2), Ashalmawia, the Shrine of Azura, Almurbalarammi, Assalkushalit, Onnissiralis, Maelkashishi and its Forgotten Galleries, Ald Daedroth Outer Shrine, Assarnatamat, Bal Fell Outer Shrine); the 7 raised trapdoors under their tower and fort hulls; the 2 Dwemer doors inside the terrain chunk; an Ald-ruhn Redoran hut door (Guard Tower 1) and the Unmarked Shipwreck's upper trapdoor. The shrine steps are the largest class: their converted collision (the expanded standing hull of curved steps) is a slope the player slides off. Fixing it changes the CHIM world's collision, so it waits for v0.0.54 with a build; config/door-check-baseline.json holds 1,067 until then.
